title: six playable characters, a picker, and the crowds built from the six (cast A, second pass)
lensAText: a sceptical game art director and UX lead. SCOPE OF THIS PASS: face realism (smudges, generic features), real hair geometry, skin shading and Marcus's scar are the queued Fable graphics pass and are NOT reasons to reject here; judge everything else. For each of the six, open the reference sheets in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/0N-name/ (body-sheet.webp, face-sheet.webp) with the Read tool and compare them with the builder's -r2 renders: at gameplay distance (picker turntable, venues, third person) is each clearly THAT person by build and height, skin tone, hair silhouette and colour, outfit and colours, shoes and accessories? Are the hard artefacts gone (beard shell or ear tabs, slipper-like boots and heels, legging trousers, ballooning sleeves, gaps, clipping, z-fighting, broken hair or cloth)? Then take your own frames in ONE short Playwright script on dist/artifact.html: the main menu's Character entry and the picker at 390x844 (phone viewport copy, DPR 3) and 1450x767; pick two different characters, walk in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (via Go To, Get out) and confirm the chosen one is on screen, the crowds use the six with visible variety and no identical copies side by side, and the driving hands take the character's skin tone and sleeves. ALSO (the owner's quality and smoothness ask): drive 60 s in the seat view steering to full lock both ways at 390x844 DPR 3 and watch for hand or arm clipping, sleeve popping, z-fighting, flicker, shimmer or stutter; check the builder's alternating frame-time table for plausibility against one short measurement of your own (CDP CPU throttle 4).
brief: SECOND PASS (2026-11-12 ~07:00 UTC). The first builder finished most of cast A on disk (uncommitted; its report is at the top of PROJECT_OC_PROGRESS.md and in PROJECT_OC_CAST.md: read both first) but stopped with done=false for three reasons; this pass settles them as follows, then the judges review the WHOLE lane. (I) CHARACTER LOOK. The faces (dark smudges on cheeks and jaw, generic features), real hair geometry, skin shading and Marcus's scar need face.ts, skin.ts, masks.ts and real hair/geometry work: that is the queued Fable graphics pass ('Fable prompt: the six characters' graphics pass' in PROJECT_OC_HANDOFF.md) and is NOT part of this pass; do not edit face.ts, skin.ts or masks.ts. THIS pass fixes the hard artefacts that live in the lane's OWN new additive code (new parameter values only; existing presets, defaults and the public API unchanged), so that each of the six reads clearly as that person at gameplay distance (picker turntable, venues, third person): (a) the full beard (Marcus, Mateo): no hard shell, no tabs at the ears, no floating edge; until the Fable pass builds strand cards, use whichever of the builder's options looks cleanest (e.g. a close-cut beard that hugs the jaw with a soft edge, or beard shading on the existing mesh without editing skin.ts/masks.ts); show before/after heads; (b) shoes: Mateo's work boots, Kate's boots, Jas's chunky sneakers, Leila's low heels and the rest must read as those shoes from the side and front (sole thickness, heel, ankle height, toe shape), not flat slippers; (c) trousers: jeans, work pants, cargo pants and tailored trousers get a straight or relaxed leg (a new fit value), not leggings; Kate's cargo pockets visible; (d) jackets, blazer, bomber, overshirt: no ballooning sleeves; the shoulder seam at the shoulder point and the sleeve tapering to the cuff; collars or lapels where the builder can; Mateo's jacket zip-front per the image; (e) Marcus reads as muscular (broad chest and shoulders, thicker arms) and the builds differ (Mateo stocky, Danny slim, Jas petite) within the builder's body parameters; (f) hair: only clear artefacts (gaps, slabs, broken strands); the 'helmet' look of the waves and side-part is the Fable pass's, but a better silhouette from the lane's own new styles is welcome if cheap. Keep the LOD budgets (phone 2,500 / 14,000 / 90,000 tris) and draw-call counts. Re-shoot all six beside their sheets (tests/cast-shoot.mjs, then tests/cast-sheets.py /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters) as -r2 images, and update PROJECT_OC_CAST.md's defect list honestly (what this pass fixed, what remains for the Fable pass). (II) SMOOTHNESS MEASUREMENT. The first pass measured on headless SwiftShader with a machine load average of 16-18: about 40 frames per 120 s desktop run, so p95 is the 3rd-worst frame and cannot resolve 10 %. Re-measure with tests/cast-perf.mjs as 3 ALTERNATING pairs (base, ours, base, ours, base, ours; base = a clean build of 5cf7212), 60 s each, on desktop 1280x720 High and on the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, CPU throttle 4); report every run and the load average. PASS = draw calls and triangles within 2 % of base, the median of the per-run p50 within +10 %, the median of the per-run p95 within +10 % OR inside the base's own run-to-run spread (state the spread), no heap growth. Any real regression (per-frame allocation, extra draws, a costly material) is fixed at its source. For the base build use a temporary detached worktree (git worktree add --detach <a folder under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/tmp-base> 5cf7212, symlink node_modules from /home/user/Claude/tsu-live/top-speed-ultra/node_modules, npm run build there) and remove it with git worktree remove afterwards; never touch tsu-live or any other worktree's files. (III) PHONE SUITE. 'sky camera: a sharp live picture inside its frame' failed in both runs. Run the full phone group on that same base build (npm test -- --only=phone in the temporary base worktree) and on ours, one after the other, not at the same time; if it fails on the base too, record it as pre-existing (not this lane's); if only ours, find the cause and fix it. Everything else in the original brief below stands, including the regression checks, the picker on the main menu, the driver match, the crowds from the six, the pack scaffold, PROJECT_OC_CAST.md and the progress entry with the table. ORIGINAL BRIEF: THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~12:30 PM PT): "make there be 6 characters to choose from 3 being male and 3 female that ChatGPT can generate images for you to accurately and realistically use for this game" (later: 'realistically' means usable, not photoreal). The owner generated the reference sheets: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/ (roster.md has the names, ages, builds, outfits and notes; each 0N-name/ folder has body-sheet.webp = front/three-quarter/side/back A-pose and face-sheet.webp = front/profile/three-quarter smile). The six: 01 Mateo Reyes (27, 175 cm, stocky), 02 Danny Tran (31, 172 cm, slim, glasses), 03 Marcus Bell (38, 188 cm, muscular, shaved head, beard, scar on his RIGHT eyebrow, sunglasses on head), 04 Leila Farahani (29, 168 cm, wavy shoulder-length hair, hoops, blazer), 05 Jas Cruz (24, 160 cm, high ponytail, cropped bomber), 06 Kate Morgan (35, 175 cm, freckles, low ponytail, denim shirt, cargo pants). BUILD: (1) src/onfoot/cast.ts (new, ours): the six as presets for the existing people builder (src/onfoot/people: buildPerson, preset, PRESETS, PersonOptions, Look, Garment, Accessories), matching the sheets as closely as the stylised real-time look allows (honest: stylised 3D on a phone, not photoreal). (2) Missing builder features, ADDITIVE ONLY, in src/onfoot/people/* (agreed with the session that owns it): new hair styles (high ponytail, low ponytail, skin fade with textured top, side-part undercut, shoulder-length waves), garments (bomber, blazer, overshirt, work jacket, henley, cargo pants, chino shorts, work pants, sandals, deck shoes, low heels, chunky sneakers, boots) and accessories (glasses, sunglasses on the head, thin chain, hoop earrings, watch, hair tie) behind NEW parameter values; existing defaults, presets and the public API unchanged; avoid face.ts, masks.ts and skin.ts (another branch changes them; if a face feature truly needs them, say so instead). (3) A character picker ON THE MAIN MENU SCREEN (owner, Nov 11 ~5:35 PM PT: 'implementing into the main menu screen too'): a prominent Character entry on the main menu showing the chosen character's portrait and name, opening the picker; also reachable from the garage. The picker: six cards with each character's three-quarter smile portrait (cropped from face-sheet.webp, compressed WebP at most ~40 KB each, inlined) plus a live 3D turntable of the selected one; the choice is saved in the profile; default = keep today's player look until the player picks. (4) The chosen character is the player's avatar on foot in Lot 57 and Stoppage Time (inside the game through src/onfoot/embed.ts, and the standalone pages), and the driving hands take their skin tone through the hands' public setTone(hex) (no edits to src/preview/hands*). Phone-cheap: LOD via the builder's own budget; no per-frame allocation. Our own names; no real brands or logos on clothing. ADD a regression check: the six presets build within budget, the picker saves and restores the choice, the venue avatar matches the choice, the hands' tone follows. PROVE: npx tsc --noEmit; npm run build (owner-test mark kept); npm test -- --only=boot,phone,venues and the new check; renders of each character front/side/back beside the same views cropped from its body sheet, and the head beside the face sheet, into tests/out/cast/; picker frames at 390x844 and 1450x767; one frame of a chosen character in each venue. THE OWNER'S MASTER BRIEF (uploaded 2026-11-11 ~1:25 PM PT; read ALL of it: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Claude/104ede24-b5bc-5131-bb4c-1bc7e86a4fd2/scratchpad/characters/MASTER_PROMPT.md) GOVERNS where it is more specific. Its IDs are technical labels; keep our names: M01 = Marcus Bell, M02 = Mateo Reyes, M03 = Danny Tran, F01 = Jas Cruz, F02 = Leila Farahani, F03 = Kate Morgan. Its 'nine PNGs' and character_roster.json were NOT attached (only the brief); we have MORE: a body sheet and a face sheet for all six (use them; do not claim any other file was inspected). Mismatches to record, not blend: Marcus's scar is on his RIGHT eyebrow in both images (text says left: follow the images); Mateo's jacket is drawn zip-front (text says open). THIS LANE (cast A) ADDS, per that brief: (5) ONE data-driven character catalog (cast.ts or a JSON it reads, in the project's own format): stable ID, name, portrait reference, the people-builder preset/params (our 'mesh and material references'), height and proportion data, wardrobe slots, animation config, unlock category ('base' for the six; 'pack' reserved). (6) NPC REUSE: the six are the ONLY human appearance archetypes for the current NPCs: rebuild Lot 57's and Stoppage Time's crowds and staff (src/onfoot/lot57/npcs.ts and crowd-worker.ts; src/onfoot/venues/sportsbar/crowd.ts, crew.ts, house.ts, life.ts; not people/*) from the six base looks with variety from wardrobe tints, compatible accessory choices, routes, schedules, idle and conversation timing, keeping each face, skin tone, defining hair and proportions recognisable, and avoid identical copies side by side; keep the crowd budgets, LODs and pooling. Honest labels ('Simulated crowd') stay. (7) A FUTURE TWO-CHARACTER PACK scaffold only: one catalog entry in src/store/catalog.json for a pair (one man, one woman), available: false, ONE configurable price with a caveat that the final price is undecided ($5 or $10 for the pair), a 'pack' unlock category in the cast catalog with NO identities shipped and nothing in the NPC pool; the store stays in test mode. (8) Write PROJECT_OC_CAST.md: the catalog and asset status (what exists: procedural presets, no imported meshes; missing pieces), mismatches, what this lane changed, verified results, the highest-impact remaining visual defects, and the next task (cast B: the full drive-park-exit-walk-enter-interact-leave-drive-reload loop and a graphics pass on the six). Extra proof for these: frames of each venue's crowd showing the six-look variety at 1280x720; the regression check also asserts the NPC pool only uses the six base looks and the pack is not for sale. (9) THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~1:30 PM PT): "make sure the driver matches to the player as well too". The game already has a driver choice: src/game/drivers.ts (DRIVERS archetypes, presentation m/f, SKINS, lookFor() -> DriverLook: skin tone, sleeve colour or rolled sleeves, gloves, watch, nails), which builds the cockpit's arms (src/game/vehicle/PlayerCar.ts buildDriverArms({look, presentation, nails, quality}) from src/preview/hands) and Lot 57's on-foot avatar (src/onfoot/lot57/driver.ts readDriver from tsu.settings). Make the chosen CHARACTER the driver everywhere, from ONE source of truth (the cast catalog + the saved choice): the cockpit arms and hands (skin tone, the outfit's own sleeves: Mateo's charcoal work-jacket cuffs, Danny's grey overshirt rolled to the forearm with his steel watch, Marcus's bare forearms below a navy short sleeve, Leila's cream blazer cuffs, Jas's olive bomber ribbed cuffs and her wrist hair tie, Kate's faded denim rolled to the elbow; nails per presentation), any driver figure visible from the hood or chase cameras, the on-foot avatar in BOTH venues (in-game mount and standalone pages), and the seat-view frames. The driver ARCHETYPE and its ability (Clear Path, Focus Time, Grip: DRIVERS in drivers.ts) stay a separate gameplay choice and work exactly as today: the character replaces only the APPEARANCE part (presentation, skin tone, outfit); the six are cosmetic and give no gameplay difference. Fold the old presentation/skin choice into the character picker (keep old saves working: map a saved presentation+skin to the closest character, documented). Bought driver styles (Night Shift, Golden Hour, Canyon Run) still apply on top (gloves, watch, sleeves) when equipped: document the rule. Use only the hands' public API (buildDriverArms options, setTone); if a sleeve or accessory the six need is missing in hands*, do NOT edit hands*: list it for the other session and use the closest existing option. Proof: seat-view frames (Day, 390x844 and 1280x720) of the hands for all six characters in the Rossini GT, and a regression assertion that the arms' look follows the chosen character. THE OWNER (2026-11-11 ~5:45 PM PT): "make sure graphics are insane for both the steering wheel and characters and make sure it doesn't have any laggy graphics or act glitchy when 1st person POV with the arms and stuff". So: (a) TOP visual quality on HD and Ultra (physically based materials with real detail: stitching, Alcantara nap, carbon weave under clear coat, brushed and machined metal, crisp emissive lines; for people: skin shading, hair shapes, cloth folds and fabric) while Low stays cheap for phones; (b) the FIRST-PERSON views with the arms (the driving seat view, and any first-person on-foot view) must be smooth and glitch-free: no hand or arm clipping through the rim, spokes or centre while steering to full lock both ways, no sleeve or wrist popping, no z-fighting or flicker on the wheel, centre or cluster, no LOD popping in view, no texture shimmer (mipmaps, anisotropy), no per-frame allocation. MEASURE IT: a 120 s seat-view drive with steering, on the phone profile (390x844, DPR 3, isMobile, Chrome DevTools Protocol Emulation.setCPUThrottlingRate 4) and on desktop 1280x720: report p50/p95/p99 frame time, long tasks over 50 ms, draw calls and triangles (window.__game stats or renderer.info) and the JS heap at start and end; the same on the base under the same conditions; the result must be no worse than +10 % p95 frame time and show no heap growth; fix any regression at its source. Put the table in the progress entry.
